extracted.intended_audience: EPA staff, regulated entities, counsel, and public commenters involved in CWA administrative penalty actions
extracted.subtask_short: petition to set aside CAFO review
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive criteria for commenters petitioning to set aside a Consent Agreement and Final Order (CAFO) under Clean Water Act sec. 309(g) and for Petition Officers/Regional Administrators deciding those petitions. Covers timeliness, materiality, Petition Officer duties, and required procedures for issuance/denial of orders and hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice and reasonable opportunity to comment before assessing penalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Before issuing an order assessing an administrative civil penalty under section 309(g), the EPA is required by the CWA and the Rules of Practice to provide public notice of and reasonable opportunity to comment on the proposed issuance of such order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations: 33 U.S.C. 1319(g)(4); 40 CFR 22.45(b)(1). This is a precondition to assessment of administrative penalties and frames who may later petition or seek a hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commenters' entitlement to notice of hearings and opportunity to be heard
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who comments on the proposed assessment of a penalty is entitled to receive notice of any hearing held under section 309(g) and at such hearing is entitled to a reasonable opportunity to be heard and to present evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations: 33 U.S.C. 1319(g)(4)(B); 40 CFR 22.45(c)(1). This protects commenters' participation rights if a hearing is convened.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to petition to set aside order when no hearing held
rubrics_metrics.description: If no hearing is held before issuance of an order assessing a penalty (e.g., where the action is settled pursuant to a consent agreement and final order), any person who commented may petition to set aside the order on the basis that material evidence was not considered and to hold a hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations: 33 U.S.C. 1319(g)(4)(C); 40 CFR 22.45(c)(4)(ii). The petition right is limited to commenters and premised on alleged unconsidered material evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality requirement for setting aside an order
rubrics_metrics.description: The CWA requires that if the evidence presented in support of the petition is material and was not considered in the issuance of the order, the Administrator shall immediately set aside such order and provide a hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materiality is thus a two-part threshold: (1) evidence must be 'material' (relevant and of enough significance to affect the outcome) and (2) it must not have been considered. If either element is missing, the petition cannot succeed. (See 33 U.S.C. 1319(g)(4)(C).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness — 30-day window to petition
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters advised they had 30 days from receipt of the Complainant's notice that the Proposed CAFO would be finalized to petition the Regional Administrator to set aside the Proposed CAFO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions must be filed within the prescribed period to be considered timely. The Federal Register notice describes a 30-day filing window in this matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition Officer's required written findings (three-part test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon review of the petition and any response filed by the complainant, the Petition Officer shall make written findings as to: (A) the extent to which the petition states an issue relevant and material to the issuance of the consent agreement and proposed final order; (B) whether the complainant adequately considered and responded to the petition; and (C) whether the resolution of the proceeding by the parties is appropriate without a hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citation: 40 CFR 22.45(c)(4)(v). These three discrete factual/legal inquiries form the core evaluation rubric for deciding whether to set aside a CAFO and order a hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition rules when Petition Officer finds hearing appropriate or not
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Petition Officer finds a hearing is appropriate, the Presiding Officer shall order the consent agreement and proposed final order be set aside and establish a schedule for a hearing. If the Petition Officer finds resolution without a hearing is appropriate, the Petition Officer shall issue an order denying the petition and stating reasons for the denial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations: 40 CFR 22.45(c)(4)(vi)-(vii). Following issuance, the Petition Officer must file the order with the Regional Hearing Clerk, serve copies on the parties and commenter, and provide public notice of the order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden on petitioner to identify material and relevant issues not considered
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner must identify material and relevant issues that were not considered by the Complainant when setting the civil penalty; failure to do so supports denial of the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this matter the Petition was denied because 'the Petitioner did not identify any material and relevant issues not considered by the Complainant when setting the civil penalty.' The petitioner's failure to point to unconsidered, material evidence is dispositive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of materiality to alleged false statements and certifications (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Alleged false statements or certifications are only material if they would affect the underlying administrative determination (e.g., the penalty calculation) or otherwise are relevant and unconsidered; merely alleging falsity or repackaging prior arguments is insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from the denial: (1) an assertedly false statement about economic benefit was held 'not material' because it would not change the economic benefit analysis; (2) an assertedly false claim of 'good faith' was held not materially false where the petitioner's evidence supported the respondent's claim; (3) an allegation that a certification was false was treated as a repackaging of prior arguments and not independently material if the underlying statements are not material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complainant's obligation to respond and the Petition Officer's review of that response
rubrics_metrics.description: When a petition is filed the Complainant is to present a written response (with exhibits) addressing the petition, and the Petition Officer reviews both the petition and the complainant's response in making findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this matter the Complainant filed a timely response with exhibits; the Petition Officer considered that response in the three-part findings required by 40 CFR 22.45(c)(4)(v). The adequacy of the complainant's consideration and response is an explicit review criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of authority to Regional Administrators for petitions in regional matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The authority to decide petitions by commenters to set aside final orders entered without a hearing and provide copies and/or notice of the decision has been delegated to Regional Administrators in administrative penalty actions brought by regional offices of the EPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This delegation (per EPA memorandum cited) affects who receives and decides petitions in regionally brought administrative penalty matters and triggers assignment of a Petition Officer under 40 CFR 22.45(c)(4)(iii).
